subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules) into Year 9; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Madd in recitation and stopping
lessons.title: Year 9 audit: tajweed in Surat Al-Kawthar
objectives: Recall the rules secured in Years 7 and 8
Find rules inside a real surah
Set two tajweed targets for the half term

keywords.def: a check of what you know and where the gaps are
reading a letter heavy, with a full mouth
clear pronunciation of noon sakinah or tanween before a throat letter

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween.
How many counts does madd lazim take?

teach.heading: Why audit?
bullets: Year 9 builds on every earlier year
Gaps in old rules slow new learning
Honest checking is part of ihsan
teach.note: Welcome pupils warmly. Explain that this half term revises madd and the lam rules, then studies three surahs. Ask: which rule do you feel least secure in? Pupils note it privately. Reassure them that the Prophet's wife A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the one who recites with difficulty has a double reward (Bukhari and Muslim). Effort matters.

teach.heading: Our text: Al-Kawthar
teach.note: Show the three ayat in Arabic: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ، فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ، إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ. Recite once yourself, then choral. Pupils should already know this surah, so the focus is rules, not memorising.

teach.heading: Rule hunt (1)
bullets: inna: noon with shaddah, so ghunnah
wanhar: noon sakinah before haa, izhar
teach.note: Model the hunt. In وَانْحَرْ the noon is sakinah and the next letter is haa, a throat letter, so izhar halqi. Ask: what would be wrong? Merging the noon into the haa. Common error: pupils nasalise the noon here.

teach.heading: Rule hunt (2)
bullets: al-kawthar: waw sakinah after fatha, no madd
abtar: stopping on raa after fatha-sad, heavy
teach.note: In الْكَوْثَرَ the waw is sakinah after fatha but a voweled thaa follows, so it is simply read, not madd leen. On stopping at أَبْتَرْ, the raa is sakin; the sakin ba before it is passed over and the fatha on the ta decides: heavy. Ask pupils to explain in their own words.

teach.heading: Set targets
teach.note: Pupils write targets in a table: rule, example ayah, how I will practise. Share two aloud. Close with a short dua asking Allah to make the Qur'an the spring of our hearts.

practice: Which rule applies to the noon in وَانْحَرْ, and why?
When you stop on أَبْتَرْ, is the raa heavy or light? Explain.
What does shaddah on noon in إِنَّا require?
independent: Recite Al-Kawthar twice, marking every rule on a printed copy
Complete the audit table: rule, secure/unsure, example
Write two targets with a practice plan
exit: Name one rule you are secure in.
Give one example ayah for a rule you want to improve.
lessons.homework: Practise your two target rules daily with five examples each from surahs you know.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: printed Al-Kawthar with rule key and colour codes. Stretch: write three audit questions for a partner.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Madd in recitation and stopping
lessons.title: Madd 'arid lis-sukun and madd leen
objectives: Explain why madd lengthens when we stop
Read madd 'arid and madd leen with 2, 4 or 6 counts
Apply both rules in Surat Quraysh

keywords.def: a madd letter followed by a letter made sakin only by stopping
waw or yaa sakinah after fatha, then a letter made sakin by stopping
one count is about one natural vowel length

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
How many counts is madd tabi'i?
Give an example of madd muttasil.

teach.heading: Stopping changes the word
bullets: When we stop, the last letter becomes sakin
A madd letter before it may then lengthen
Only at the stop, never when continuing
teach.note: Write الْعَالَمِينَ on the board. Continue: the last noon has fatha, madd letter yaa is 2 counts. Stop: noon becomes sakin, so yaa is followed by a sakin letter and may be 2, 4 or 6. Ask: when does this rule apply? Only when you actually stop.

teach.heading: Madd 'arid lis-sukun
bullets: Madd letter, then last letter sakin by stopping
teach.note: Take Al-Fatihah ayat. Stop on نَسْتَعِينْ and stretch evenly. Key rule: keep the same length through the whole recital. Misconception: pupils choose a random length each time. Say 4 and keep to 4, or 2, or 6.

teach.heading: Madd leen
bullets: Waw or yaa sakinah, fatha before it
Next letter sakin only because we stop
teach.note: Use Surat Quraysh: قُرَيْشٍ, الْبَيْتِ, خَوْفٍ. Stopping on خَوْفْ: the waw sakinah after fatha, then the faa sakin by waqf. Pupils feel the lips stay gently relaxed. Contrast with continuing: خَوْفٍ is read plainly.

teach.heading: Spot the difference
bullets: Madd 'arid: long vowel letter before the stop
Madd leen: waw/yaa sakinah after fatha
teach.note: Quick sort on screen: الْعَالَمِينَ, الْبَيْتِ, يَوْمِ الدِّينِ, خَوْفٍ. Pupils drag into 'arid or leen. Check reasons, not just answers. Common error: calling any waw or yaa sakinah a madd leen even when no stop follows.

teach.heading: Recite Quraysh
bullets: Choose a length and keep it
teach.note: Pupils recite Quraysh in pairs choosing 2, 4 or 6 counts for every stop. The partner ticks consistency. Circulate and praise accurate stops. The surah Quraysh is 106 and has four ayat.

practice: Stop on الْعَالَمِينَ. Which madd applies and how many counts?
Stop on قُرَيْشٍ. Why is it madd leen?
Read الْبَيْتِ continuing: is there any extra madd?
independent: Sort 12 words into madd 'arid, madd leen or neither
Recite Al-Fatihah stopping on every ayah ending with 4 counts
Recite Quraysh with a consistent length, partner checks
exit: Why is madd 'arid only found when we stop?
What makes a madd leen different from a madd 'arid?
lessons.homework: Mark every madd 'arid and madd leen on Surat Quraysh and recite it daily.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: two-colour card (blue = arid, green = leen) with six sample words. Stretch: explain to a partner why the length must stay consistent.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Madd in recitation and stopping
lessons.title: Madd silah and madd 'iwad
objectives: Read the pronoun haa with silah sughra and silah kubra
Read tanween fatha at a stop with madd 'iwad
Find both rules in Surat Al-Humazah and Surat An-Nasr

keywords.def: lengthening of the pronoun haa (hu, hi) joined to the next word
tanween fatha becomes an alif when we stop
the hamzah that is always pronounced

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Name two kinds of madd far'i from Year 7.
Which madd takes six counts?

teach.heading: Pronoun haa and silah
bullets: The haa meaning 'him/his' is between two vowels
It is read with a small waw or yaa
Silah sughra: 2 counts before a normal letter
teach.note: Show لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ. The haa has damma, the letter before it has a vowel, and the next letter has a vowel. So it is read as lahū. Misconception: pupils shorten it. Condition checked: vowel before, vowel after.

teach.heading: Silah kubra
bullets: Same haa, but a hamzat qat' comes next
teach.note: Ayah 104:3 يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ. The haa is followed by hamzah of أَخْلَدَهُ. Stretch 4 or 5 counts like madd munfasil. Another example: عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا in Ayat al-Kursi (we study that in Year 10).

teach.heading: When there is no silah
bullets: No silah if the letter before haa is sakin
No silah if the next letter is sakin
Hamzat al-wasl after haa: no silah
teach.note: Contrast فِيهِ هُدًى (ya sakin before haa, no silah) with the rule. Give a short list; a few Qur'anic words are exceptions (for example in Surat Al-Furqan), and your teacher will show you when you meet them. Do not overwhelm pupils with exceptions.

teach.heading: Madd 'iwad
bullets: Stop on tanween fatha, not on taa marbutah
teach.note: Say: when continuing we say hakeeman; when stopping we say hakeemaa. Examples: 4:17 ends عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا, and 110:3 ends إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا. Taa marbutah (like رَحْمَةً) stops as a sakin haa, no alif.

teach.heading: Practice in Al-Humazah
teach.note: Pupils read 104:3 and 110:3 aloud, then partner tick. Misconception: applying madd 'iwad to rounded taa. Collect errors and review them together.

practice: In مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ, is this silah sughra or kubra? How many counts?
Why is there no silah in فِيهِ هُدًى?
How is تَوَّابًا read when you stop?
independent: Sort 10 words into silah sughra, silah kubra, no silah
Recite Surat An-Nasr stopping on every ayah
Write two sentences explaining madd 'iwad to a younger pupil
exit: Name the two conditions for silah sughra.
What happens to tanween fatha when you stop?
lessons.homework: Find two more examples of the pronoun haa in your mushaf and decide silah sughra or kubra.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-coded cards showing vowel + haa + vowel. Stretch: find a word with haa that has no silah and explain why.

lessons.title: Alif-lam: shamsiyyah and qamariyyah
objectives: Read al- with the lam pronounced or merged
Sort the 14 sun letters and 14 moon letters
Apply to Surat Al-'Asr and Al-Fil

keywords.def: lam of al- merges into a sun letter, so it is not pronounced
lam of al- is pronounced clearly before a moon letter
doubling mark on the sun letter

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Which letters are throat letters?
What does a shaddah mean?

teach.heading: The definite article
bullets: The lam changes before some letters
teach.note: Write ٱلشَّمْسُ and ٱلْقَمَرُ. Recite both. In the first, no lam is heard; in the second it is clear. The names mean 'sun' and 'moon' and teach the rule. Ask: what do you notice about the letter after the lam?

teach.heading: Sun letters (14)
bullets: ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن
Lam merges into the sun letter
teach.note: Say the sun letters in order. Examples: as-salihat, an-nar, ar-Rahman, as-sabr. Misconception: pupils think the lam is deleted; actually it merges and the letter is doubled. Practise chorally.

teach.heading: Moon letters (14)
bullets: ا ب ج ح خ ع غ ف ق ك م ه و ي
teach.note: Examples: al-'asr, al-haqq, al-fil, al-hutamah, al-af'idah. Ask pupils to find two moon examples in Al-'Asr and Al-Fil. Remember that the lam is sakin and pronounced; no merging.

teach.heading: Check by sight
bullets: Look for shaddah on the next letter
teach.note: Show mushaf lines with and without the sign. In printed mushafs the lam of shamsiyyah usually has no sukoon and the next letter has shaddah. Quick-fire: pupils shout 'sun' or 'moon'.

teach.heading: Lam in Allah
bullets: After fatha or damma: heavy lam
teach.note: Link to Year 7 raa and laam. الله after fatha/damma: heavy, e.g. قَالَ اللَّهُ. After kasra: light, e.g. بِسْمِ اللَّهِ. Pupils recite both. Common error: heavy lam after kasra.

practice: Sort: الشَّمْسُ، الْقَمَرُ، النَّارُ، الْحَقِّ، الصَّبْرِ، الْفِيلِ
Why is the lam not heard in الصَّالِحَاتِ?
Is the lam in اللَّهِ heavy after kasra? Explain.
independent: Sort 20 words from Al-'Asr, Al-Fil and Al-Humazah into sun and moon
Recite the same words using the correct lam sound
Create a memory aid for the 14 sun letters
exit: Name three sun letters.
How can you tell shamsiyyah from qamariyyah by sight?
lessons.homework: Learn the 14 sun letters and 14 moon letters by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sun and moon letters on a colour card. Stretch: find five examples in Surat Al-Baqarah and classify them.

lessons.title: Hamzat al-wasl: starting well
objectives: Recognise hamzat al-wasl and hamzat al-qat'
Choose the correct vowel when starting on hamzat al-wasl
Practise starting mid-ayah

keywords.def: a joining hamzah, pronounced only when starting
a cutting hamzah, always pronounced
starting a recitation or restarting after a stop

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What is a moon letter?
Give a word with a shaddah.

teach.heading: Two kinds of hamzah
bullets: Hamzat al-wasl is silent when joined
It has an alif without a hamzah sign
teach.note: Compare أَنْعَمْتَ (qat') with اهْدِنَا (wasl). In وَقَالَ اهْدِنَا we drop the wasl. When joining, the hamzah disappears; only when you start do you say it. Ask: why does Arabic have a joining hamzah? For ease of speech.

teach.heading: Start with fatha
bullets: In ال, the start vowel is fatha
teach.note: Starting on ٱلْحَمْدُ gives 'Alhamdu'. Do not say 'ilhamdu'. Pupils rehearse starting at Al-Fil ayah 1 and Al-'Asr ayah 3 (illal-ladhina uses a qat' hamzah, a different case).

teach.heading: Start with kasra or damma
bullets: Verbs: look at the third letter
Third letter has damma: start with damma
teach.note: Count the alif as first letter. ٱدْعُ: third letter 'ayn has damma, start with damma, ud'u. ٱهْدِنَا: third letter dal has kasra, so ihdina. ٱقْرَأْ: third letter ra has fatha, so start with kasra: iqra'. Practise chorally.

teach.heading: Nouns and special words
bullets: Starting on ism: say ism, with kasra
teach.note: Short list of nouns with hamzat al-wasl: ibn, ibnah, ism, ithnan, imra'ah. Starting on 'ism' we say ism with kasra. These are rare, so stress recognising rather than memorising everything today.

teach.heading: Practise starting
teach.note: Teacher names an ayah; pupils start there. At Al-Fatihah ayah 6 (ihdinas-sirat) the start is kasra. For Al-Fil ayah 2 start with 'Alam' (qat'). Correct errors with kindness.

practice: Is the first hamzah in اهْدِنَا wasl or qat'? How do you start?
Starting with ٱدْعُ: which vowel and why?
How do you start the word ٱبْن?
independent: Sort 12 words by hamzat al-wasl or qat'
Start at five ayat chosen by your partner
Write the third-letter rule in your own words
exit: How do you start the word ٱقْرَأْ?
Does the hamzah of ٱهْدِنَا get pronounced when joined?
lessons.homework: Find five words in Juz' Amma that begin with hamzat al-wasl and note the starting vowel.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: flow chart (verb? third letter damma? yes/no). Stretch: explain why the hamzah is silent when joined.

lessons.title: Surat Al-'Asr: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-'Asr accurately
Identify rules in each ayah
Stop and start correctly

keywords.def: time, or the late afternoon
loss
they advised one another

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Kawthar from memory.
Is the lam in الْعَصْرِ shamsiyyah or qamariyyah?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
teach.note: Recite: وَالْعَصْرِ، إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ، إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. Surah 103. Pupils repeat after you in short chunks. This surah is short but dense with meaning.

teach.heading: Ayah 1 and 2 rules
bullets: khusr: stop on sakin raa, heavy
teach.note: Ayah 2: إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ. The alif of al- is hamzat al-wasl and drops when joined, so we say innal-insana, with ghunnah on inna. The hamzah of insan is a moon letter, so the lam is clear. At the stop خُسْرْ, raa is sakin after sakin sin; the vowel before them is damma on kha, so heavy.

teach.heading: Ayah 3 rules
bullets: illal-ladhina: lam merges, shaddah on laam
teach.note: Be precise: آمَنُوا has hamzah then madd letter in the same word: this is madd badal, normally read at 2 counts. Do not call it muttasil. Ask pupils what the difference is: in muttasil the hamzah comes after the madd letter.

teach.heading: Ayah 3, second half
teach.note: Point out the final alif after waw in تَوَاصَوْا is not pronounced. The waw is sakin after fatha. Stop on الصَّبْر: raa sakin, ba sakin before it, sad has fatha so tafkhim. Ask pupils to say it with a full mouth.

teach.heading: Stopping points
bullets: Start again at the next ayah
Do not stop in the middle of a phrase
teach.note: Remind pupils that stopping at ayah ends is the best practice. Starting mid-ayah is allowed if breath runs out, but go back to a sensible word. Practise one stop in the middle of ayah 3 after وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ and restart.

practice: Which type of lam is in الْعَصْرِ?
Why is the raa heavy when you stop on خُسْرٍ?
Is آمَنُوا madd muttasil or badal? Explain.
independent: Recite Al-'Asr three times, marking each rule
Record yourself and listen back
Peer assess using the checklist
exit: Name two rules in ayah 3.
How do you stop on الصَّبْر?
lessons.homework: Memorise Surat Al-'Asr securely and recite it to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio support, chunked lines. Stretch: add explanations of each rule in writing.

lessons.title: Surat Al-'Asr: meaning and reflection
objectives: Explain the oath and the four conditions
Link the surah to daily life
Reflect on how we use our time

keywords.def: a solemn statement swearing by something
faith
patience and steadfastness

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-'Asr.
What does khusr mean?

teach.heading: The oath by time
bullets: 'Asr means time, or the late afternoon
teach.note: Explain that Allah swears by what He wills, and that scholars mention both time and the late afternoon as meanings. Do not claim one only. Ask: what does swearing by time tell us about its value?

teach.heading: Humanity in loss
teach.note: Stress the 'unless'. The exception that follows shows that loss is not the final answer. Ask: where do we see loss in life? Wasted time, wasted talent, wasted chance. Keep this simple and uplifting.

teach.heading: The four conditions
teach.note: Write the four in order on the board and tie each to the Arabic: آمَنُوا، عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ، تَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ، تَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. Note that the last two are community actions: we do not rescue ourselves alone.

teach.heading: Living the surah
teach.note: Ask pupils to give one example of 'tawasaw bil-haqq' (a friend reminding you to pray) and 'tawasaw bis-sabr' (encouraging a friend to continue revising). Discuss how to give advice gently. Link to the idea that Muslims support one another.

teach.heading: Tadabbur steps
bullets: Ask: what does it ask of me?
teach.note: Teach a three-step tadabbur routine: say it, understand it, apply it. Note that this is a reflection method, not a replacement for a scholar's tafsir. Pupils write one personal action.

practice: What does Allah swear by in the first ayah?
List the four conditions that save from loss.
Why is advising one another so important?
independent: Draw a four-part diagram of the four conditions with an example for each
Write a short paragraph: how I will use my time better
Discuss in pairs: how to give advice with kindness
exit: Name the four conditions.
Give one action you will take from this surah.
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word reflection on Surat Al-'Asr and one practical goal.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: word bank for the four conditions. Stretch: compare the surah with 49:11 on respect between believers.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Humazah: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Humazah (104)
Identify noon, tanween and meem rules
Stop and restart sensibly

keywords.def: one who slanders or backbites
changing noon sakinah to a meem when ba follows
merging two identical letters

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-'Asr.
Name the iqlab letter.

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: Pupils echo, then recite in pairs
teach.note: Recite: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ، الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ، يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ، كَلَّا لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ... Keep a measured pace; this is a heavy surah to hear. Maintain a calm tone.

teach.heading: Noon and tanween
teach.note: Show examples: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ (tanween before lam: idghaam bila ghunnah), مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ (tanween before waw: idghaam bi-ghunnah), لَيُنبَذَنَّ (noon before ba: iqlab). Ask pupils to say why. Misconception: using ghunnah on lam.

teach.heading: Meem and silah
teach.note: عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ: meem sakin followed by meem with shaddah, merge with ghunnah. عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ: tanween then meem. مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ: silah kubra, 4-5 counts. Revise these from Lesson 3.

teach.heading: Hard words
teach.note: Practise الْحُطَمَةِ, تَطَّلِعُ, الْأَفْئِدَةِ slowly. In تَطَّلِعُ the taa is doubled with the taa that follows (tatta-li'u). Pupils pronounce the doubled sound firmly. Check each shaddah is held clearly.

teach.heading: Stops
bullets: On mumaddadah: stop with a sakin haa
teach.note: The last ayah ends in a taa marbutah with tanween kasra, so we stop on a sakin haa: mumaddadah. The same for al-hutamah in ayah 4. Remind pupils of the difference from tanween 'iwad. Practise restarting at ayah 4.

practice: Which rule is in لَيُنبَذَنَّ?
Which rule joins عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ?
How do you stop on مُّمَدَّدَةٍ?
independent: Recite ayat 1-5 and mark every noon and meem rule
Recite ayat 6-9 with a partner
Self-assess with the checklist
exit: Name one iqlab word in the surah.
Why is there silah kubra in مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ?
lessons.homework: Learn ayat 1-5 of Al-Humazah and recite them tomorrow.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and colour key. Stretch: teach the rules to a partner.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Humazah: meaning and adab with speech
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah
Connect the surah with respectful speech
Reflect on attachment to wealth

keywords.def: a severe warning of destruction
speaking about someone in a way they would dislike
the Crusher, a name for a place in the Fire

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite ayat 1-5.
What is idghaam mithlayn?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3: the warning
bullets: Humazah and lumazah: those who slander and mock
He gathers wealth and counts it again and again
teach.note: Explain that humazah and lumazah both refer to harming people with words, and that scholars give slightly different distinctions; keep it simple. The surah goes on to wealth: counting and hoarding. The next ayah: he thinks his wealth will make him last forever.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-9: the consequence
bullets: He will be thrown into al-Hutamah
It will be closed over them in extended columns
teach.note: Read the translation slowly. Emphasise that these are strong words which should make us reflect, not frighten us for no reason. Ask: what is the link between the first three ayat and these ones?

teach.heading: The tongue
teach.note: Read the meaning of 49:11: let not a people mock another people. And 49:12: do not spy on one another or backbite. A hadith in Sahih Muslim defines ghibah as mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes. Discuss: why is it hard to avoid backbiting?

teach.heading: Wealth and the heart
bullets: Wealth is a test, not a goal
Gratitude and generosity are the cure
teach.note: Avoid saying wealth is bad. The surah criticises hoarding and false security. Ask pupils how generosity might be the opposite. Link to Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur from Year 8.

teach.heading: My personal action
bullets: One word I will stop using
One kind word I will say daily
A dua for a clean tongue
teach.note: Pupils write their action privately. No sharing is required. Close with a dua for protecting our tongues and our hearts from harm.

practice: What does humazah mean?
What false belief does the person have in ayah 3?
Which ayah of Surat Al-Hujurat forbids backbiting?
independent: Write a one-paragraph tafsir summary of ayat 1-4
Create a 'Think before you speak' checklist
Discuss in pairs: when is it okay to mention someone's fault? (advice, not gossip)
exit: Give two meanings of the surah in your own words.
State one action to protect your tongue.
lessons.homework: Write about one situation where you can practise kind speech this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simple translation chart with key words. Stretch: compare with Surat Al-Ma'un in 150 words.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Fil: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Fil (105)
Identify rules in each ayah
Practise stops and hamzah

keywords.def: flocks of birds
hard baked clay
dry chaff or leaves

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Humazah.
What is iqlab?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
teach.note: Recite: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ، أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ، وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ، تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ، فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍ. Model slowly.

teach.heading: Noon and tanween rules
teach.note: طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ: tanween then hamzah, so clear. حِجَارَةٍ مِّن: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah. مِن سِجِّيلٍ: noon sakin before sin, ikhfa. Ask why. كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍ: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah.

teach.heading: Soft yaa in kayfa and kaydahum
bullets: Yaa sakinah after fatha is a leen letter
teach.note: كَيْفَ and كَيْدَهُمْ have yaa sakinah after fatha. Madd leen only appears when the next letter is sakin because we stop. Here the next letter has its own vowel, so no lengthening. Ask: how is this different from stopping on قُرَيْشٍ?

teach.heading: Madd and the end
teach.note: Stopping on تَضْلِيلٍ: madd 'arid. Stopping on مَأْكُولٍ: waw madd followed by lam sakin by stop, so 2, 4 or 6. Recall consistency. Mention the hamzah in مَأْكُولٍ is a hamzah sakinah after meem fatha.

teach.heading: Self-check
teach.note: Pupils read, partner marks. Teacher circulates. Listen for the doubled jeem in سِجِّيلٍ, the clear kaf in كَيْفَ and the heavy letters in طَيْرًا and تَضْلِيلٍ.

practice: Which rule applies to طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ?
Which rule applies to مِن سِجِّيلٍ?
Stop on مَأْكُولٍ. Which madd, how many counts?
independent: Recite Al-Fil three times, marking each rule
Record a recitation and compare with a model
Peer assess with the checklist
exit: Name two noon/tanween rules in Al-Fil.
What is sijjil?
lessons.homework: Learn all of Surat Al-Fil securely.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio chunks and rule key. Stretch: explain every rule aloud for ayah 4.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Fil: meaning and lessons
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah
Describe the historical setting without adding detail the Qur'an does not give
Draw out lessons about trust in Allah

keywords.def: the people of the elephant
plan or scheme
relying on Allah while taking the means

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Fil.
What is idghaam bi-ghunnah?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-2: Do you not see?
bullets: Alam tara: have you not seen?
Allah dealt with the people of the elephant
Their plan was brought to nothing
teach.note: Explain that the question is for the Prophet ﷺ and for us to reflect on. The Qur'an says Allah made their plan go astray (fi tadlil). Ask: what is a scheme? What does it mean for it to fail completely?

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5: What happened
bullets: They struck with stones of baked clay
He made them like eaten-up chaff
teach.note: Stay with the Qur'an's wording: tayran ababil, hijaratin min sijjil, ka'asfin ma'kul. Do not add details such as the shape or size of the birds, since the surah does not give them. Ask: what image does 'chaff' create?

teach.heading: Historical setting
bullets: Seerah sources name Abrahah and his army
They marched against the Ka'bah in Makkah
This became known as the Year of the Elephant
teach.note: Say clearly that Abrahah's name comes from historical (seerah) sources, not from the Qur'an text. Well-known tradition says the Prophet ﷺ was born in that year. Separate what the Qur'an says from what reports add. Ask: why does this distinction matter?

teach.heading: Lessons
bullets: Allah protects His House and His religion
Power and numbers are not everything
Trust Allah and do what is right
teach.note: Discuss tawakkul: relying on Allah while taking the means. Ask pupils for an example from daily life (revising and making dua). Link to Surat Quraysh which follows Al-Fil in the mushaf, which reminds Quraysh to worship the Lord of this House.

teach.heading: Reflect
bullets: Where do we meet arrogance today?
How should we respond with humility?
A dua for protection and humility
teach.note: Pupils write one sentence on pride versus humility. Keep discussion general, not political. Close with a dua asking Allah to protect us and keep our hearts humble.

practice: What does 'fi tadlil' mean?
Name two details the Qur'an gives about the birds' attack.
Does the Qur'an name the leader of the army? Explain.
independent: Write a summary of each ayah in your own words
Draw a storyboard of ayat 3-5
Write a short paragraph on tawakkul
exit: What is one lesson from Al-Fil?
What is the difference between what the Qur'an says and what history adds?
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word reflection linking Al-Fil and Quraysh.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture-supported translation. Stretch: compare Al-Fil with another surah on divine protection.

lessons.title: Recital assessment and reflection
objectives: Recite one chosen surah from the half term with accuracy
Self-assess and peer-assess against the rubric
Set targets for Year 10

keywords.def: a set of criteria for judging quality
reading smoothly without hesitation
a clear goal for improvement

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Fatihah.
Which surah will you recite today and why?

teach.heading: Prepare
bullets: Check noon, meem and madd rules
Take a calm breath and begin
teach.note: Give pupils five minutes to prepare quietly. Remind them of adab: calm, clean place, a dua. Reduce nerves with encouragement and remind them of the hadith narrated by A'ishah that the one who struggles in recitation has a double reward.

teach.heading: Rubric
teach.note: Share the rubric with levels. Pupils recite individually in breakout rooms or in the main room. Mark with the rubric. Stress that the teacher gives one strength, one target and one action.

teach.heading: Recite and listen
teach.note: In pairs, pupils recite, then listen. Use sentence stems: 'One strength was...', 'One target is...'. Keep the atmosphere supportive.

teach.heading: Revision plan
teach.note: Show a simple revision cycle: new, recent, old. Pupils write a plan for the next two weeks. Link this with Year 8's long-term memorisation work.

teach.heading: Reflect
teach.note: Pupils write a short reflection. Share one thing aloud. Close with a dua for sincerity, steadfastness and love of the Qur'an.

practice: Which rule is most secure for you?
Which rule needs more work?
independent: Recite your chosen surah for assessment
Complete peer feedback with the rubric
Write a reflection and three targets
exit: Name one strength.
Name one target for Year 10.
lessons.homework: Practise your targets daily and record a new recitation next week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simplified rubric with sentence stems. Stretch: coach another pupil on one rule.
